title: Systems and automation in Tucson, Arizona | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs consolidates spreadsheets and disconnected tools into one system for Tucson businesses, builds internal tools, and automates repetitive work.
intro: Many Tucson businesses run on a mix of tools that were adopted one at a time: QuickBooks for invoicing, Google Sheets or Excel for scheduling and job tracking, a shared inbox for customer requests, and an industry system such as Jobber, Housecall Pro, Clio, or Buildium for part of the work. Contractors, clinics, property managers, and professional firms often re-enter the same customer, job, or client data in 3 or 4 places. Systems and automation applies wherever that duplication exists.

Creosote Labs consolidates those spreadsheets and disconnected tools into one system of record for a Tucson business, builds the internal tools it needs for scheduling, quoting, tracking, and reporting, and automates the data entry, follow-up, and document generation that staff currently do by hand. Work begins with a one-day operations review at $3,000 that produces a written assessment and a quote for each recommendation. Every system we build is documented and handed over to staff.
projects: A job tracker for a Tucson roofing company that replaces 3 spreadsheets and produces work orders, material lists, and invoices from one record.
An automated follow-up sequence for a plumbing company that sends estimate reminders and review requests from Jobber data.
A tenant maintenance request system for a property management company that logs requests, assigns vendors, and posts updates to AppFolio.
A monthly status dashboard for an accounting firm that pulls client progress from a practice tracker into a single view.
A parts and inventory tracker for a small manufacturer that replaces an Excel workbook and flags reorder points.

faqs.q: How long does the operations review take and where does it happen?
faqs.a: The review takes one day and happens on site at the business in Tucson. The written assessment, prioritized recommendations, and quotes arrive within the week.

faqs.q: What do we need to provide before the review?
faqs.a: The business provides access to the spreadsheets and systems it currently uses, and time with the people who use them. We document how the business runs today before recommending any changes.

Implementation is quoted from the operations review as a fixed price for each recommendation. There is no hourly billing, and the $3,000 review fee is credited toward implementation that begins within 90 days.
